notes:
Summary/notes from calls and syncs:
- Company: mid-market SaaS (B2B customer engagement platform). Productized chat assistants embedded in web and mobile. Heavy concurrent chat sessions during business hours (peak ~180-220 rps).
- Primary evaluation path: start Hosted API for dev + pilot -> Dedicated (reserved) when steady throughput and cost predictability needed. Team keeps asking: "If we move to Dedicated, can we keep same API and rollout policies?" Need one-liner confirmation.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 <=150ms (NA), <=200-220ms (EU). Streaming for token-by-token UX (client expects sub-200ms initial token, then smooth stream). Tool calling: webhooks + connector to internal DB (low-latency fetches) — needs synchronous function-calls and retry/backoff semantics.
- Routing/fallback requirements: must route NA requests to NA region by default, fall back to EU if NA capacity saturated only after failing over to a smaller model variant. Also want per-tenant pinning and emergency fallback to a lightweight model for graceful degradation.
- Cost sensitivity: product team cares about per-conversation cost; finance wants ARR estimate and an example bill for 250k messages/mo. Trying to balance quality vs token cost (interested in recommended quantization & batching profiles).
- Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML), audit logs for API calls, KMS integration for key management, and written confirmation of EU data residency options (logs & token storage).
- Quote from CTO on 2026-01-19 call: "We need streaming to feel instantaneous. If p95 slips beyond 200ms EU, product stickiness drops."
- Internal POC plan: 2-week soak with synthetic traffic (180 rps peak), run canary traffic to hosted API NA + EU, validate smart-routing and KV cache hit rates, capture trace-level latency.
- Sales notes: bring a sample Reserved (Dedicated) 6mo pricing sheet and a simple migration checklist. Provide clear SLOs and runbook for failover.
- Next immediate action: deliver POC runbook + EU region latency report template by 2026-02-17.
